children: Questions About Interactive Prototyping Worth Asking Before You Start

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-a77620d e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

props.aria-label: Accordion. Open links with Enter or Space, close with Escape, and navigate with Arrow Keys

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-5c03b07 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: The process of building a clickable, navigable representation of a digital product before development begins. An interactive prototype simulates how a product looks, behaves, and responds to user input without requiring production code to be written. It is the tool that answers product questions at the stage when answers are cheapest to act on.
What is the difference between a wireframe and a prototype?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-1fd69c6 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: A wireframe is a static layout that shows structure and hierarchy without interaction. A prototype is a clickable, navigable artefact that simulates real user flows. A wireframe shows what a product looks like. A prototype shows how it behaves. Both have a place in the design process — the question is which one the current decision requires
What is the difference between a low-fidelity and a high-fidelity prototype?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-4d7fde7 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: A low-fidelity prototype uses rough, unpolished layouts to validate structure and flows. It is fast to build and fast to change. A high-fidelity prototype uses pixel-accurate screens and detailed interactions to simulate the real product experience. Low-fidelity is right for early structural decisions. High-fidelity is right when the audience needs to evaluate the product rather than the concept.
How much does a prototype cost?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-de35b03 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: A focused low-fidelity prototype for early concept validation starts from $3,000. A high-fidelity interactive prototype for investor demos or development handoff typically ranges from $8,000 to $25,000, depending on the number of screens, interaction complexity, and animation requirements. The precise scope and cost are defined in the Brief and Scope stage before build begins.
How long does it take to build a prototype?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-9e70e62 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: A low-fidelity wireframe prototype takes one to two weeks. A high-fidelity clickable prototype with full interaction states and animation typically takes two to four weeks. The timeline depends on the number of user flows, the fidelity level required, and how many iteration cycles are needed to validate the question the prototype was built to answer.
Can a prototype be used for investor presentations?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-959b826 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: Yes. A high-fidelity prototype that behaves like the real product is one of the most effective tools in an investor presentation because it gives the audience something to interact with and evaluate rather than something to imagine from a slide. Every flow in an investor demo prototype is scripted around the decisions the audience needs to make, not around a complete product walkthrough.
Do I need a prototype before development begins?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-8614664 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: Not always. A prototype is the right investment when there is a specific question about user behavior, interaction logic, or product concept that development cannot answer without building first. If the design is validated, the flows are confirmed, and the development team has a clear specification, a prototype may not be necessary. The Brief and Scope stage determines whether prototyping is the right next step for your specific situation.
How does a prototype transition into a development handoff?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-5174f60 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: A validated prototype transitions into a development handoff through annotated Figma files, component specifications, interaction documentation, and animation exports. Every interaction state, edge case, and responsive behavior is documented so the development team builds what was tested rather than what was assumed. For prototypes built in Framer, the React component structure can transition directly into the development codebase.
